title: Support CSS Overflow Module Level 5
impact: 7 reactions, filed by a maintainer-team member. Duplicates: #1072 (::scroll-button) and #1177 (::scroll-marker). Users of Chrome's CSS carousel pattern get one warning per selector, and build tools that promote warnings to errors fail. The output itself is already correct: the selectors pass through unchanged in both modes.

summary: The :target-current/before/after pseudo-classes already landed in #1185 behind the `drafts.scrollNavigationControls` flag. ::scroll-marker, ::scroll-marker-group, ::scroll-button() and ::column are still unknown pseudo-elements. Today they warn in both strict and errorRecovery mode but pass through unchanged, so no errorRecovery bug. The properties (scroll-marker-group, scroll-target-group) pass through silently as unparsed. Only Chrome ships this (since 135, all 'experimental' in BCD). Mozilla (#1161) and WebKit (#447, concerns about accessibility and i18n) have no position. The ED still has open syntax issues on ::scroll-button() keywords. Recommendation: implement behind the existing draft flag. Open PR #1321 does that, but misses ::scroll-button():disabled, which the spec explicitly allows.

Chromium 153 CSS.supports: ::scroll-button(*):disabled true, ::scroll-marker:target-current true, ::column::scroll-marker true, ::scroll-button(next) false, ::scroll-button(sideways) false. css-overflow-5 Overview.bs is Status: ED, with an inline Issue about adding multi-button keywords (all/horizontal/vertical/block/inline) to ::scroll-button(). It also says "The ':disabled' pseudo-class can apply to '::scroll-button()'". Standards positions: mozilla/standards-positions #1161 (CSS Overflow Navigation Controls), #1251 (scroll-target-group) and #1291 (:target-before/after) are open with no position; WebKit/standards-positions #447 is open with concerns: accessibility and internationalization, #514 and #544 are open.

fix.approach: Behind ParserFlags::SCROLL_NAVIGATION_CONTROLS: add ScrollMarker, ScrollMarkerGroup and ScrollButton{direction}, plus ::column. Allow :target-* after ::scroll-marker, and :disabled/:enabled after ::scroll-button(). Add mdnFeatures to build-prefixes.js. Properties can stay unparsed for now, or get typed parsers later. The JS AST change only adds new union cases.

openPRs.assessment: Recommend reviewing it, with one change requested. It adds the three pseudo-elements behind the existing flag, adds the compat features via build-prefixes.js (not hand-edited), has tests, and only adds AST cases. Gap: with the flag on, `::scroll-button(*):disabled` (allowed by the spec and accepted by Chromium; the common carousel pattern) would hit InvalidPseudoClassAfterPseudoElement. That is an error in strict mode, and errorRecovery would drop the rule. It needs the same AFTER_* exception as ::scroll-marker. Also missing: ::column (and ::column::scroll-marker). Its `prev`/`next` keywords are in the ED, but no browser supports them. Mergeable state: behind master. Closes #1177.

draftReply:
Status update: `:target-current`, `:target-before` and `:target-after` shipped in 1.33.0 behind `drafts: { scrollNavigationControls: true }`. There's an open PR, #1321, that adds `::scroll-marker`, `::scroll-marker-group` and `::scroll-button()` behind the same flag. Until then, these selectors are passed through unchanged with a warning. They stay behind a flag because only Chrome ships them so far, Mozilla and WebKit haven't taken positions (mozilla/standards-positions#1161, WebKit/standards-positions#447), and the draft still has open questions on `::scroll-button()` keywords. #1072 and #1177 track the same thing.
